name: Area burnt by wildfires
descriptionShort: Area burnt by [wildfires](#dod:wildfires) in hectares. The 2026 data is incomplete and was last updated 07 August 2026.
descriptionKey:
- Wildfires are detected through the use of satellite imagery obtained from MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite). These satellite systems are capable of identifying thermal anomalies and alterations in landscape patterns, which are indicative of burning.
- The data provider is presently engaged in a global accuracy assessment and acknowledged that they might be underestimating the genuine impact of wildfires, primarily due to constraints imposed by the spatial resolution of the sensors they employ.

values.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

origins.title: Seasonal wildfire trends
origins.descriptionSnapshot: This dataset covers all years from 2003 up to and including the current year.
origins.description:
The dataset provides a weekly comprehensive overview of fire activity and its environmental impact, incorporating data from the Global Wildfire Information System (GWIS) and satellite imagery from both MODIS and VIIRS. It includes metrics such as the area of land burnt, cumulative burnt areas, carbon dioxide emissions from fires, cumulative carbon emissions, the number of fires, and cumulative fire counts.

It draws on two satellite sensors: MODIS (1km resolution, available from the early 2000s) and VIIRS (375m resolution, available from 2012). VIIRS's finer resolution means it picks up smaller fires that MODIS misses. Because the combined record only extends back to 2012, this dataset is best suited for tracking the current fire season and recent trends rather than long-run historical comparisons.
